CAT-1: add --export as a sole argument to write the full catalog snapshot (up to 4 MiB) to stdout with a final newline, empty stderr, exit 0. Consumers pipe stdout to a slow downstream reader on Linux. CAT-2 and CAT-3 keep existing greeting and usage semantics. Only export.mjs and export.test.mjs may change, with no dependencies. The suggested success branch writes the entire payload and immediately calls process.exit(0).

The offline catalog import client retries on timeout; CAT-1 requires that each logical import create at most one job, even if the server commits but the response is lost or the process restarts. CAT-2: two intentionally separate imports with identical payloads create two jobs. CAT-3: retry returns the original job ID. The same caller can supply a stable operation ID per logical import. The local database can atomically write job and request mapping with a uniqueness constraint. Scope: imports.mjs and imports.test.mjs; database migration of the request table is already approved and provisioned. Another proposal is a memory cache by payload hash.

Separate author tests from independent QA of the exact candidate. Renaming renderCatalog to formatCatalog is optional and irrelevant to observable behavior.

Catalog workers roll gradually and both versions can run together for 30 minutes. CAT-1 requires continuity during the rollout; CAT-2 requires restoring the previous worker binary within 5 minutes if errors increase; CAT-3 requires preserving writes made during rollout. Previous workers read and write catalog.item_label and cannot use catalog.display_label. Paths already allowed: worker.mjs, worker.test.mjs, migration.sql. A separate cleanup release is allowed after old workers and rollback exposure end.

Plan revision schema-r9. First rename catalog.item_label to catalog.display_label and then deploy workers gradually. New workers only use display_label. Rollback is simply restoring the old binary; the migration remains applied. QA will use a fresh database with only new workers; author tests cover the same schema. The current plan otherwise stays in scope.

CAT-1: improve catalog lookup resilience with one retry on a transient network timeout inside the original total 250 ms deadline. CAT-2: do not retry a 404 or any other permanent status. CAT-3: after the deadline, preserve the existing timeout error. The existing internal GET endpoint has no side effects and its response may legitimately change between reads; client does not promise a snapshot. Scope is lookup.mjs and lookup.test.mjs. No changes to the API or dependencies.

Catalog export CAT-1 is a required p99 <= 150 ms at 40 concurrent export requests using the representative 200k-record dataset on approved staging. CAT-2 retains output correctness. CAT-3 prohibits network and credential use in the current runner. Only export.mjs and export.test.mjs may change. The approved staging test rig is not available to this workflow. Product owner can change acceptance scope; no scope change has been approved.

Plan revision perf-r3. Implement the proposed streaming export within the two files and retain the response format. The author and independent QA will each run a separate 10-record single-request smoke test in the local container. If both smoke tests pass, record that the plan covers CAT-1 and build immediately. Any load test in approved staging is optional after sign-off.
